migrate-verify-to-executor-contract, fix-artifacts: review recommendation 3, part (e), needs a design decision before the remaining spec deltas can be written.

The conflict: tasks 3.3/3.6 and design D4 turn the GitHub check adapter into the `github-actions` built-in verdict executor and register it in `ExecutorRegistry` (bootstrap). The main spec `openspec/specs/plugin/github-plugin/spec.md:9-38` promises the github tracker AND check providers are discovered through ServiceLoader and that there is 'no privileged built-in shortcut'; `GithubPluginAbsenceSpec.groovy:31` fails any production source outside `adapters/github/` that names a `Github[A-Z]` type, so a bootstrap registration breaks an existing spec. design.md weighs no alternative for this. The same choice decides the text of the still-missing MODIFIED blocks: plugin-discovery (ServiceLoader for 'tracker and check', the four-point criterion for the check port), plugin-api-contract 'Thin plugin-api contract module', pipeline-config 'Local sanity validation' (scenario 'Defaulted github provider absent from the registry'), github-external-check 'Adapter is constructed from factory configuration'.

Already applied this round (valid, strict + merged-spec checks green): R1 (built-in usage REPORTED, D13), R2 (new D14: the resuming instance's program executor adopts the recorded key, before-view taken at adoption; MODIFIED wire-contract 'Poll of a program is refused...' and 'A pending judge is judged when it ends'), R3 parts a/b/c/g/h (http, stage model, stateless polling, pin-check), R4 (operator config factory.executors.<name>, inline or connection: profile), R5, R6. Override D14 or R4 in your answer if you disagree.

Options:
A) Core-registered built-in: github-actions is registered by core like `command`; MODIFY github-plugin to cover the tracker only (removing the jar disables the github tracker; github-actions stays), move the executor's source out of adapters/github or narrow GithubPluginAbsenceSpec's scan under the decision; plugin-discovery and plugin-api-contract restated for the tracker port only.
B) Discovered executor provider: the github jar contributes its github-actions executor through a new ServiceLoader SPI (executor provider) the registry loads beside the law's declarations and core built-ins; github-plugin stays true with one wording change; adds a type to gnomish-plugin-api (M4 'no check SPI type' must then be read as 'no check-specific SPI') and a third registry source (D8 of define-executor-contract: registry = law + built-ins).
C) github-actions leaves the factory: shipped as an external verdict program (script/image) declared in the law like any third-party verifier; no built-in, no SPI; FR6 and D4 change from 'built-in' to 'reference program'.

My recommendation: A — it matches the change's stated intent (FR6, D4: built-ins; Why: the GitHub poller's sibling is the git remote, not the tracker plugin) and keeps FR8/M4 as written; B re-creates an in-process Java plugin path the change exists to remove.
options: A: core-registered built-in, github-plugin narrowed to the tracker
B: discovered executor-provider SPI from the github jar
C: github-actions becomes an external reference program
